name: French Onion Smothered Pork Chops

dupe_check.against_catalog_digest: Not a dupe. Nearest pork neighbor is 'southern-smothered-pork-chops-and-rice' (chicken-broth, flour, heavy-cream, onions, pork-chops, rice): that is a Southern flour/cream onion-gravy chop served over rice, a starch-based dinner. This candidate is caramelized-onion + beef stock + sherry + melted Swiss with no starch (8g carbs). Same protein and skillet method, but different sauce family (French onion caramelized+cheese vs Southern cream gravy) and different starch (none vs rice) - distinct dish.
dupe_check.against_accepted_slugs: No collision; accepted-slugs.json holds no pork chop and no French onion dish as of this reading.
dupe_check.against_pork_pool: No other French onion or smothered-cheese pork chop seen in this adjudicator's handful.

cross_protein_collision_flags: French-onion flavor family already lives in the catalog as OTHER proteins: 'slow-cooker-french-onion-chicken-bowls' (chicken) and 'french-onion-pot-roast-bowls' (beef). Both are bowl/starch formats; this is a low-carb bone-in chop, so not a dupe - but decider should watch for a same-dish French-onion-PORK twin (e.g. a French onion pork chop or French onion pork bowl) arriving from another selector's pool.
Structurally this is the 'protein + caramelized onion + beef stock + melted cheese' French-onion template; the chicken-bowls version is its closest cross-protein cousin.
